questions.question:
I. The first inscription evidence of Sati is found during the Satavahana period.
II. The Eran Pillar Inscription of Bhanugupta in Madhya Pradesh mentions the practice of Sati.
III. Raja Ram Mohan Roy described Sati as murder and helped in the passing of the Bengal Sati Regulation Act, 1829.
questions.solution:
I only
Earliest inscription evidence of Sati is from the Gupta period, not the Satavahana period.

questions.question: The famous source of the Gupta empire, the Prayaga Prashasti is also known as the _______.
questions.solution:
Allahabad pillar inscription
Composed in Sanskrit by Harishena, the court poet of Samudragupta.

questions.question: Who was the court poet of Harshavardhana?
questions.solution:
Banabhatta
His teacher's name was Bhatsu or Bhavru. Banabhatta's three works are famous - "Harshacharita", "Kadambari" and "Chandisthak". Harshavardhana was the ruler of the Pushyabhuti dynasty of Thaneshwar.

questions.question: Who among the following Navratnas from Chandragupta II court wrote 'Mantrashastra'?
questions.solution:
Vetala Bhatta
Nine jewels (Navratna) of Chandragupta II - Amarasimha, Dhanvantari, Harisena, Kalidasa, Kshapanaka, Shanku, Varahamihira, Varuchi, Vetala-Bhatta.

questions.question:
Arrange the following Gupta rulers in chronological order of their reign:
I. Chandragupta I
II. Samudragupta
III. Chandragupta II
IV. Kumaragupta I
questions.solution:
I → II → III → IV
  • Chandragupta I (c. 319-335 CE) - Founder of the Gupta dynasty's imperial line; married Kumaradevi of the Licchavi clan
  • Samudragupta (c. 335-375 CE) - Known as the "Napoleon of India"
  • Chandragupta II (c. 375-415 CE) - Also called Vikramaditya; period marked as the Golden Age of the Gupta Empire
  • Kumaragupta I (c. 415-455 CE) - Known as Shakraditya/Mahendraditya; founded Nalanda Mahavihara; succeeded by Skandagupta

questions.question: Which king was shown on his coins as a Veena player?
questions.solution:
Samudragupta
He was a ruler of the Gupta dynasty. On several of his coins, he was depicted as seated on a sofa and playing a Veena. He is known as the Napoleon of India. He was given the title of Kaviraj.

questions.question: After the victory over Sakas, who among the following adopted the title of 'Vikramaditya'?
questions.solution:
Chandragupta II
He was the son of Samudragupta and Datta Devi. He ruled the Gupta Empire from 380 to 415 AD during the Golden Age of India. He established the Mehrauli iron pillar.

questions.question: Who among the following succeeded Ghatotkacha, the Gupta ruler?
questions.solution:
Chandragupta I
Founder - Sri Gupta, Next Successors - Ghatotkacha, Chandragupta I, Samudragupta, Chandragupta II, Kumaragupta I (founded Nalanda University).

questions.question: Ruler of which dynasty built the famous Iron pillar in Delhi?
questions.solution:
Gupta dynasty
In Mehrauli (Delhi) an iron pillar was constructed by the famous king Chandragupta II, notable for the rust-resistant composition of the metal used in its construction. The inscription on the pillar is in Sanskrit, about Gupta emperor Chandragupta II.

questions.question: Which of the following offices was NOT held by the poet Harishena?
questions.solution:
Nagara-shreshthi (Chief banker or merchant)
Offices held by Poet Harishena: Maha-danda-Nayaka (Chief Judicial Officer), Kumar-amatya (Important minister) and Sandhi-vigrahika (Minister of War and Peace).

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Fa Xian's journey to India:
(A) Fa Xian, the Chinese traveller, came to India to acquire Buddhist texts.
(B) He arrived in India during the reign of Chandragupta II and reached Pataliputra from the northwest.
(C) Fa Xian began his journey back home from Bengal by boarding a merchant ship.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
A, B and C
Fa Xian came to India primarily to collect Buddhist texts and study Buddhism. He visited India during the reign of Chandragupta II and reached Pataliputra from the northwest. Fa Xian returned to China from the Bengal region by ship.

questions.question: Samudragupta's mother belonged to which of the following gana?
questions.solution:
Licchavi
Samudragupta (335-375 CE, Kaviraja) was the son of Chandragupta I and Queen Kumaradevi (Licchavi clan). He is called 'Napoleon of India' by V.A. Smith.

questions.question: In the context of Gupta administration, the term 'vithi' referred to a/an:
questions.solution:
Administrative unit
In Gupta period, there was a hierarchy of administrative divisions from top to bottom. The empire was called by various names such as Rajya, Rashtra, Desha, Mandala, Prithvi, and Avani. It was divided into provinces, which were further divided into Vishayas. A Vishayapati administered the Vishaya. A part of the Vishaya was called Vithi.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Chandragupta I married a princess from the Licchavi clan to strengthen his political power.
Reason (R): The Licchavi clan was headquartered at Vaishali in present-day Bihar.
questions.option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.option_3: A is true, R is false
questions.option_4: A is false, R is true
questions.solution:
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
Reason is factual but not the direct reason for the political purpose of the marriage.

questions.question: Which of the following plays was NOT written by Harshavardhana?
questions.solution:
Vikramorvasiyam
Vikramorvasiyam is a romantic play written by Kalidasa, based on the legend of King Pururavas and an Apsara named Urvashi. Kalidasa's works include: Abhijnanasakuntalam, Malavikagnimitram, Kumarasambhavam, Vikramorvashiyam, Raghuvamsha, Meghadutam.

questions.question: Pulakeshin II assumed the title of 'Dakshinapatheshvara' (lord of the south) after defeating which of the following rulers of north India?
questions.solution:
Harshavardhana (606-647 AD)
Harshavardhana belonged to the Pushyabhuti dynasty, also known as the Vardhana dynasty. He wanted to extend his power in the Deccan but he was defeated by Pulakesin II, the Chalukya ruler, on the bank of river Narmada. The river thus became the southern boundary of his kingdom. Vardhana dynasty: Founder - Pushyabhuti. Capital: Thanesar (Thaneshwar), later Kannauj (Kanyakubja).

questions.question:
With reference to the Pushyabhuti (Vardhana) dynasty, consider the following statements:
A. The Pushyabhuti dynasty rose to prominence in northern India after the decline of the Gupta Empire.
B. Prabhakarvardhana strengthened the dynasty's position in Punjab and Haryana after defeating the Hunas.
C. The capital of the dynasty was Ujjain.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
A and B only
The Pushyabhuti dynasty, also known as the Vardhana dynasty, established its power in present-day Haryana with Sthanishvara (Thaneshwar) as its capital, not Ujjain. After defeating the Hunas, Prabhakarvardhana consolidated the dynasty's rule in Punjab and Haryana. The dynasty later reached its zenith under Harshavardhana (606-647 CE).

questions.question: Thaneshwar where the Vardhana dynasty ruled around the present-day state of
questions.solution: Haryana

questions.question: According to which of the following foreign travellers did Dhruvasena II attend Harsha's assembly at Prayag (Allahabad)?
questions.solution:
Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang)
Chinese Buddhist monk who travelled from China to India to study Buddhism and obtain Buddhist scriptures during the reign of King Harsha Vardhan. Assembly of Prayag (Maha Moksha Parishad) - Harsha Vardhan gave all his belongings in charity for the welfare of the public.

questions.question: Who sent an envoy to the Chinese court in 641 AD?
questions.solution:
Harsha Vardhan
In 641 AD Harshavardhan sent an envoy to Taizong (Tai-Tsung), the Tang emperor of China and in return, the Chinese ruler sent three embassies to Harsha court.

questions.question: After about 75 years of Harshavardhana's death ______ rose to power in Kannauj.
questions.solution:
Yashovarman
He was the founder of the Varman dynasty of Kanauj and surrounding areas during the 8th and the 9th centuries.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Harshavardhana:
A. He ruled from 606 CE to 647 CE.
B. He authored three Sanskrit plays - Nagananda, Ratnavali, and Priyadarshika.
C. His capital was Kannauj from the very beginning of his reign.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
A and B only
Harshavardhana initially ruled from Thaneshwar; he later shifted his capital to Kannauj. His reign is well-documented by the Chinese traveler Hiuen Tsang and his court poet Banabhatta (author of Harshacharita).

questions.question: Which Chola ruler is credited with the construction of irrigation systems to support agriculture?
questions.solution:
Rajendra Chola I
To commemorate his victorious expedition to the Gangetic plains, he built a new capital called Gangaikonda Cholapuram. Near this capital, he created a colossal artificial lake, an irrigation tank named Cholagangam. This engineering marvel, described as a liquid pillar of victory, was fed by canals to irrigate vast tracts of land in the surrounding areas.

questions.question: Which Chola ruler is credited with the extensive overseas expedition to Southeast Asia, particularly against the Srivijaya Empire?
questions.solution:
Rajendra Chola I (1014-1044 CE)
Son of Rajaraja Chola I, is known for:
  • Naval campaign (1025 CE): Defeated Srivijaya Empire, controlling Southeast Asian trade routes
  • Title "Gangaikonda Chola": Earned after his northern expedition up to the Ganga
  • Expanded Chola power across India and Southeast Asia
Kulothunga I - Known for administrative reforms. Vijayalaya Chola - Founder of the Chola dynasty revival in the 9th century. Rajaraja I - Expanded Chola empire in India and parts of Sri Lanka, but overseas expeditions to Srivijaya were led by his son Rajendra.

questions.question:
With reference to medieval history, consider the following statements.
1. The founder of the Chola dynasty called the 'Imperial Cholas' was Vijayalaya (9th century AD).
2. One of the important dynasties which ruled in northern India was Gurjara-Pratiharas.
3. Palas ruled in western India and Rashtrakutas ruled in southern India in the early years (750-1000).
Which of the given statement(s) is/are correct?
questions.solution:
1 and 2 only
The successors of Vijayalaya expanded the Chola kingdom by annexing Pandyan and Pallava territories. Rajaraja I, who became king in 985, strengthened and reorganized the empire. His son, Rajendra I, further extended the Chola influence with expeditions to the Ganga valley, Sri Lanka, and Southeast Asia, supported by a powerful navy. Palas ruled in eastern India and Rashtrakutas ruled in the Deccan region.

questions.question: One of the greatest of Chola rulers, Rajaraja I ruled from 985 AD to
questions.solution:
1014 AD
The Chola Empire was founded by Vijayalaya. Rajaraja I was known for his conquests of South India and parts of Sri Lanka. He built the great Brihadisvara Temple at the Chola capital Thanjavur.

questions.question: Which of the following animals was the emblem of the Chola dynasty?
questions.solution:
Tiger
Three dynasties ruled during the Sangam Age:
  • Cheras: Modern-Day City (Kerala), Ancient Capital (Vanji), Important Ports (Musiri, Tondi), Emblem (Bow and Arrow)
  • Cholas: Modern-Day City (Tamil Nadu), Ancient Capital (Uraiyur, Puhar), Important Ports (Kaveripattinam), Emblem (Tiger)
  • Pandyas: Modern-Day City (Tamil Nadu), Ancient Capital (Madurai), Important Ports (Muziris (Muchiri), Korkai, Kaveri), Emblem (Carp/Fish)

questions.question: Brihadisvara Temple of Tanjore was built by which of the following Chola emperors?
questions.solution:
Raja Raja Chola
The Brihadisvara Temple (Dravidian-style) also known as Raja Rajeswara Temple is dedicated to Shiva. It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987.

questions.question: Which among the following Chola emperors defeated the Pandya king Maravarman Rajsimha II in the battle of Vellore?
questions.solution:
Parantaka I
Rajaraja I, the son of Parantaka II, is the most celebrated of the Chola kings and ascended the throne in 985 AD. Rajendra I, the son of Rajaraja I, became the first Chola king to venture to the banks of the Ganges, earning the title "Victor of the Ganges."
